top5.why: Only owner (the cross-chain manager) gates replacement of the consensus keeper keys; hijacking it lets an attacker forge cross-chain proofs.
Releases locked assets for any message the manager forwards, trusting only manager identity and a bytes-equal proxy hash.
Ownership of the data contract controls the keeper key set, so ownership change is the crown-jewel privilege.
Owner can redirect which manager is trusted to call unlock.
Owner-set proxy hash is the only check that the source-chain contract is legitimate in unlock.
Exchange rate derived from raw cash balance and totalSupply is vulnerable to donation inflation and rounding on empty or new markets.
Collateral valuation multiplies manipulable exchange rate by oracle price with truncation.
Skips liquidity check for non-member accounts, allowing redeem/borrow ordering abuse.
Auto-enters market and relies on oracle plus liquidity check; credit-limit branch bypasses liquidity check.
Seize amount depends on manipulable exchange rate and oracle prices.
Public function lets any caller pass _slippageOverride (unbounded) so amountOutMinimum can be near zero, enabling sandwiching of the reward swap; also relies on a TWAP quote.
Triggers swap of entire paired-LP balance on every share change with default slippage, exposing it to manipulation.
Rewards per share accounting when totalShares is tiny can be skewed and rewards burned.
Transfers reward token to wallet during share updates before state fully settled in some paths.
Entirely trusts the tracking token to report share changes.
Permissionless launch forwards attacker-supplied initCalldata/modifyCalldata to the position manager multicall as the factory, which owns all launch NFTs, enabling theft of other positions.
Uses attacker-controlled token/pairedStock and balance diffs; positionIdOf can point at another position; pushes funds to holder list.
Executes caller-supplied preCommands/preInputs on the universal router using factory approvals and balances.
Unbounded loop over holders with external transfers to a possibly malicious reward token.
Attacker can bloat holderList with dust holders, making harvest gas-expensive or revert.
Unprotected function lets anyone pass an arbitrary devaddr and router, moving 80% of that account's balance into the contract and then to an attacker-chosen LP recipient.
Balance changes are decided by an external router call instead of the amount, so balances are controlled outside the token.
Allowance enforcement happens after the router-driven _transfer and amounts are not tied to input.
Router address is decoded from stored bytes and used as a trusted external call target.
Standard approve, listed as low-probability fallback.
Executes arbitrary module transactions on the safe once the oracle answer is positive; relies on bond, cooldown and tx index checks that can be gamed.
Question re-asking and invalidation logic can be abused to replace or resurrect proposals.
Permissionless invalidation path based on oracle result and finalize timestamp.
Public wrapper around executor-only invalidation.
Question id computation must exactly match oracle to prevent substitution.
No reentrancy guard; Curve pool LP valuation read during withdrawal can be manipulated through read-only reentrancy to mis-price the exchange rate.
Computes exchange rate from Curve LP prices before and after deposit with no reentrancy guard, enabling read-only reentrancy.
Total underlying is derived from oracle prices of Curve LP tokens whose virtual price can be manipulated mid-callback.
Converts LP balance using an oracle price that may be manipulated through Curve reentrancy.
Removes liquidity from Curve pools, giving the attacker an ETH callback while pool state is inconsistent.
Pays full pending rewards for all matured deposits on every withdrawal without marking them claimed, so repeated small withdrawals drain the reward pool.
Reward calculation has no claimed-state tracking so matured deposits keep yielding the same reward.
Feeds unclaimed-agnostic reward amount into withdraw.
Swap-and-pop deposit removal and tier handling alter positions while rewards are computed.
Owner can withdraw all staked funds.
Tick-crossing and liquidity accounting in the swap loop can mis-handle the boundary between target price and tick, double-counting liquidity.
Final sqrt price rounding with reinvestment liquidity can misprice swap output.
Step logic decides usedAmount and reached-target state that drives tick crossing.
Computes amount needed to reach the target price with fee scaling and rounding.
Applies liquidity net on tick cross; inconsistencies with currentTick can corrupt liquidity.
